newsitem.title: POLAND: Daewoo unit to borrow $200 mln in Poland - paper.
newsitem.headline: Daewoo unit to borrow $200 mln in Poland - paper.

text.p: South Korean Daewoo Group's car-making subsidiary Daewoo-FSO plans to borrow up to $200 million in Poland this year, Gazeta Wyborcza on Thursday quoted the firm's financial director as saying.

Janusz Lach told the daily that Daewoo-FSO in Warsaw's Zeran suburb planned spending of up to $650 million, of which $550 million would be used this year for production of the new Lanos model and $100 million for other purposes.

"We have spoken of our investment plans and needs at a meeting with about 80 financial institutions operating in this country, banks, insurance companies and leasing firms," Lach was quoted as saying.
"Daewoo will contribute $220 million in the form of machinery, equipment and money. In June we will get $100 million in cash from Daewoo," he said.

A further $200 million is to come from credits supplied by trading companies which will provide the Zeran plant with machinery, leaving about $200 million which the Korean parent aims to raise within Poland, Gazeta Wyborcza reported.
Lach said last month Daewoo planned to invest $2.215 billion in the automotive industry in Poland by the year 2001.
Investment in its plant in the south-eastern town of Lublin would total $500 million by 2001 and another $215 million in the engine plant Andoria in the town of Andrychow.
Maciej Motelski, head of Daewoo-FSO's production, said that by 2001 investment in Daewoo-FSO would total $1.5 billion of which one third would be spent in 1996-1997.
Assembly of the new Lanos model is to start in September 1997 with full production in Poland beginning in March 1998.
